items.stem: What is the main advantage of a driver-based forecast over a line-item forecast?

options.text: It links outputs to business assumptions you can test and update
options.rationale: Correct: drivers make the forecast explainable and quick to flex.

options.text: It is always more accurate in every period
options.rationale: No forecast guarantees accuracy; drivers aid insight and agility.

options.text: It removes the need for actuals
options.rationale: Actuals are still needed to validate drivers.
It frames uncertainty; it does not remove it.

items.explanation: Correct: drivers make the forecast explainable and quick to flex.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Revenue was below plan. Which TWO analyses best isolate why? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: it separates rate effects from quantity effects.

options.text: A customer or product mix analysis
options.rationale: Correct: shifts in mix can move revenue even at planned prices and volumes.
Historical statutory accounts do not explain this period's miss.
That is a data structure change, not variance analysis.

items.explanation: Correct: price/volume and mix analyses isolate the drivers of the miss.

items.stem: A board pack shows 40 metrics with no commentary. The main FP&A weakness is:

options.text: No prioritisation or narrative to support decisions
options.rationale: Correct: effective reporting highlights the few metrics that drive decisions and explains them.

options.text: Too few metrics to be useful
options.rationale: The problem is too many, unprioritised metrics.
KPIs are appropriate; the issue is focus and narrative.
Leading indicators are valuable when chosen deliberately.

items.explanation: Correct: effective reporting highlights the few metrics that drive decisions and explains them.
